clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of deviation scores (general linear model); relative importance analysis to rank contributions of clinical variables (LD, ADHD, handedness, sex, CSS); Pearson correlations between individual atypicality scores and symptom severity scores (ADI-R, ADOS-2), with FDR correction.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Individuals with autism show highly individualized patterns of extreme right- and leftward brain asymmetry deviations, which are associated with symptom severity and language delay, suggesting that atypical lateralization is a potential stratification marker.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Compared to neurotypical controls, individuals with autism showed significantly more extreme rightward (p < .001) and leftward (p < .001) deviations from the normative model of brain laterality. These deviations were highly individualized with minimal spatial overlap. Language delay (LD) was the largest contributor to extreme rightward deviations, while core autism symptom severity (CSS) was the largest contributor to extreme leftward deviations. Individuals with autism and LD showed a stepwise increase in rightward deviations compared to those without LD and controls. A significant correlation was found between extreme rightward deviations and ADI-R communication scores (r = .14). Findings were replicated in the ABIDE dataset.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Limitations include small subsample sizes after stratification (by site, sex, LD); potential for residual site effects despite correction; the cross-sectional design, which precludes analysis of developmental trajectories; and the modeling approach may be less sensitive to detecting reduced laterality (i.e., a lack of specialization) compared to extreme deviations.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, despite the large dataset, when dividing individuals by diagnostic group, sex, LD, and site, subsamples decrease substantially in size... Second, large datasets come at the expense of additional confounds associated with site... Third, the question arises whether there are also experience-dependent in /uniFB02 uences on cortical asymmetry. Longitudinal analyses are needed... Fourth, the normative modeling approach is suitable for detecting extreme deviations from a normative pattern. However, an alternative hypothesis that individuals with autism might lack specialization of either hemisphere (68), which would be expressed in reduced laterality, might be less detected with the current approach.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study contrasted the normative modeling results with a conventional voxel-based case-control analysis (PALM), which yielded no significant group differences, highlighting the value of the individual-level approach in heterogeneous populations.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study performed extensive robustness checks, including re-running analyses after using ComBat for site correction, including handedness as a regressor, using FDR correction on the Z-score maps, controlling for IQ/handedness/SES, excluding individuals with IQ < 70, and analyzing only right-handed subjects. The primary findings remained robust across these sensitivity analyses.
